title: Layerwise Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Quantum Clients using Quorus
claim: Distributed clients with heterogeneous hardware quality must collaborate through a central server despite running models of different depths.
layout: Single row, server left and clients right, looping arrows, legend box right
description: A horizontal system diagram. On the left, a purple box labeled 'Parameter aggregation server' shows a computer monitor and server rack icon with an 'atan2 Σ' label. To its right are five green client boxes (Client 1–5, then an ellipsis), each with a different quantum-chip icon. Above each client is a stack of colored parameter blocks (cyan, yellow, red, green) of varying length, which represents circuits of different depths. A top line labeled 'Share parameters over a classical channel' runs from the clients to the server with an arrow. A bottom line labeled 'Receive aggregated parameters over a classical channel' runs from the server back up to each client with arrows. A dashed legend box on the right explains green as Quantum Computer and purple as Classical Computer. It also notes that clients vary and must run circuits of different depths. The eye goes first to the purple server and the green clients.
caption: Depiction of the overall setup of our depth-heterogeneous quantum FL framework. Our setup utilizes the realistic scenario of a classical network for sending and receiving parameters, and each client has a quantum computer that can run circuits of varying depths.
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) holds the promise to solve classically intractable problems, but, as critical data can be fragmented across private clients, there is a need for distributed QML in a quantum federated learning (QFL) format. However, the quantum computers that different clients have access to can be error-prone and have heterogeneous error properties, requiring them to run circuits of different depths. We propose a novel solution to this QFL problem, Quorus, that utilizes a layerwise loss function for effective training of varying-depth quantum models, which allows clients to choose models for high-fidelity output based on their individual capacity. Quorus also presents various model designs based on client needs that optimize for shot budget, qubit count, midcircuit measurement, and optimization space. Our simulation and real-hardware results show the promise of Quorus: it increases the magnitude of gradients of higher depth clients and improves testing accuracy by 12.4% on average over the state-of-the-art.
